evals.name: no_anchor_blocks_the_artifact
evals.prompt: I want an agent that keeps improving our onboarding docs every week. Success is when the docs feel clearer. Write me the loop.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to emit an artifact until an anchor exists; explains that 'feel clearer' cannot be argued against and so the loop cannot tell progress from motion; proposes a candidate anchor such as a measured support-ticket count or a doc lint, and returns to that question instead of writing the prompt.

evals.name: phase_split_is_refused
evals.prompt: Set up four agents for this feature: one plans, one implements, one writes tests, one reviews. Give me the workflow script.
evals.expected_output: Refuses splitting by workflow phase because each phase needs the previous phase's context and handoffs degrade it; names the cheap alternative (one agent for the slice plus one independent verifier); does not simply comply with the four-node script.

evals.name: self_review_is_refused
evals.prompt: The loop should check its own work at the end of each iteration and stop when it is satisfied.
evals.expected_output: Rejects both halves: a generator grading itself praises its output, and an agent-owned definition of 'satisfied' drifts toward whatever ends the turn. Requires a fresh-context verifier and an owner-defined quantified stop condition with a turn ceiling.

evals.name: unquantified_stop_condition_is_sharpened
evals.prompt: Stop condition: keep going until the test suite is in good shape.
evals.expected_output: Converts it into an anchor command plus an exact threshold plus a turn ceiling; explains that a ceiling is required or an unreachable threshold runs until someone notices the cost.

evals.name: loop_is_enough_so_no_graph
evals.prompt: One agent needs to fix a failing test: read the error, open the file, patch it, re-run. Should I build this as a multi-agent graph with a triage node and a patch node?
evals.expected_output: Keeps it as one loop; notes that the routing cannot be drawn in advance because the next step depends on the error, and that extra agents cost 3-10x tokens plus another failure point. Emits a goal package, not a workflow script.

evals.name: graph_is_allowed_when_context_isolates
evals.prompt: I need three independent audits of the same module - overflow, reentrancy, gas - each needing different reference material. Must I prove one agent fails first?
evals.expected_output: Allows the graph without requiring a prior single-agent failure, because context genuinely isolates and the paths are independent; assigns each worker its own anchor and defines the integration rule and total budget.

evals.name: cross_vendor_star_limits_are_stated
evals.prompt: Four vendor agents each run their own loop and feed each other, and I coordinate. Write the delegation package.
evals.expected_output: Names the shape as orchestrator-worker star rather than a mesh: delegation is blocking request/response with no shared state, no checkpoint, and no worker-to-worker channel, so every edge passes through the orchestrator and each mission must be self-contained. States the re-delegate-versus-visibility trade-off explicitly.

evals.name: heterogeneous_models_for_independence
evals.prompt: For cross-review, should I run three copies of the same model with different prompts, or three different vendors?
evals.expected_output: Chooses different vendors where independence is the point, because agents differ only by context, scaffolding, and underlying model, so identical agents make identical mistakes and agreement between them is one opinion counted repeatedly.

evals.name: single_worker_delegation_is_a_loop
evals.prompt: Here is my graph: one worker agent, delegated from me, running until done.
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as a loop rather than a graph and emits a goal package; does not dress a single delegation up as a topology.

evals.name: mutual_checking_without_ground_is_refused
evals.prompt: Every agent reviews another agent's output and the orchestrator reads all the reports. That is fully verified, right?
evals.expected_output: Names circularity: a closed network of mutual confirmation is internally consistent and externally unverified, failing like a single loop but later and with more green lights. Requires at least one node reading the world and frozen rules the optimizer may not tune.

evals.name: single_metric_gets_a_counter_metric
evals.prompt: The loop optimizes ticket resolution rate weekly. Metric is clear and measurable, so we are fine.
evals.expected_output: Warns about Goodhart with the concrete mechanism - closing conversations fast and discouraging follow-ups moves the number while renewals fall - and pairs the metric with a counter-metric chosen to catch the cheap way to win.

evals.name: decisions_record_is_not_architecture
evals.prompt: Also write a design doc describing the nodes, the edges, and the data flow so we can keep it up to date.
evals.expected_output: Declines a prose copy of the topology: the script or prompt is the only description, and a second copy goes stale and starts lying. Offers the three-column decisions record instead, and says that revising a decision edits the row rather than appending history.

evals.name: artifact_ends_with_a_start_command
evals.prompt: Fine, we settled everything. Give me the loop.
evals.expected_output: Emits the paired artifact and decisions record at the project's workflows path, runs the validator, and hands off with the exact command to start it plus what the first iteration should produce - without running it unasked.

evals.name: one_shot_task_does_not_activate
evals.prompt: Rename this function and update its callers.
evals.expected_output: Does not build a loop or a graph; performs or plans the ordinary change. The Skill's machinery stays out of a one-shot task.

evals.name: existing_artifact_makes_it_a_modify
evals.prompt: Set up an agent that keeps our dependencies patched.
evals.expected_output: Checks the workflows directory before asking anything, finds the artifact that already covers dependency patching, and treats the intent as Modify - reporting what exists and asking what should change - instead of running a fresh interview and writing a second artifact for the same job.

evals.name: modify_surfaces_a_rejected_decision
evals.prompt: Make the upgrade loop merge the PR automatically when the build is green.
evals.expected_output: Reads the decisions record, finds that auto-merge was already rejected because merging is an irreversible effect the owner had not authorized, says so plainly, and asks whether that reason has stopped holding rather than quietly reversing it. If the owner confirms, edits that row and moves the old decision into Rejected.

evals.name: inspect_changes_nothing
evals.prompt: What loops do we have and what state are they in?
evals.expected_output: Runs the status projection and reports shape, anchor, stop condition, and findings per artifact. Writes nothing, edits nothing, and does not start an interview.

evals.name: running_anchors_needs_consent
evals.prompt: Just tell me whether all of them are currently passing.
evals.expected_output: Explains that answering it means executing the commands the artifacts name in a shell, asks for the owner's go-ahead before using --run-anchors, and does not execute anything unasked.

evals.name: changed_anchor_reopens_the_interview
evals.prompt: Actually the real measure is customer-reported incidents, not the test suite. Update the loop.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that the anchor itself changed rather than a detail, and reopens the interview instead of editing a row - a loop whose anchor changed is a different loop. Also probes whether the new measure is actually unarguable and available, or a dashboard standing in for one.

evals.name: state_is_not_tracked_in_a_file
evals.prompt: Add a state file that records each loop's current status so we can query it fast.
evals.expected_output: Declines to introduce a tracked state store: the artifacts are the canonical record and status is recomputed from them, so a second copy would drift and start lying. Points at the status projection instead.

evals.name: unattended_loop_needs_carry_over
evals.prompt: Set up a weekly loop that keeps our dependencies patched. Here is the anchor and the stop condition.
evals.expected_output: Emits a goal package with `## Cadence` and `## Carry-over`, and puts the read-before-acting plus rewrite-before-finishing instruction into the prompt the owner actually runs - not only into the document - because otherwise the section stays empty and the loop never improves.

evals.name: one_shot_goal_needs_no_carry_over
evals.prompt: I want a one-off goal: keep going until the failing test passes, then stop.
evals.expected_output: Emits a goal package without cadence or carry-over. A loop that runs once and is watched has no next iteration to carry anything to; adding the sections would be ceremony.

evals.name: carry_over_is_rewritten_not_appended
evals.prompt: Append this iteration's findings to the carry-over section so we build up a full record.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to append: rewrites the section to what is still true and deletes what is not. Explains that a section which only grows has become a log, that Git already holds the history, and that the section's whole value is being short enough to read at the start of every iteration.

evals.name: history_belongs_to_git
evals.prompt: I want to be able to see how this loop evolved over time. Add a changelog section to the document.
evals.expected_output: Declines the changelog and points at version control: `git log -p <slug>.goal.md` is the evolution at full fidelity and `git log --oneline` is the trajectory. Recommends committing once per iteration with a one-line summary, which is what puts the evolution in Git and is why the document holds only current truth.

evals.name: raw_trace_stays_out_of_the_repository
evals.prompt: Also save each iteration's full agent transcript into the repo so nothing is lost.
evals.expected_output: Declines: one iteration's raw trace is tens of thousands of tokens of tool calls that no human will read, and committing it bloats the repository to store what the commit message and the anchor result already summarize.

evals.name: lesson_stays_in_the_project
evals.prompt: This loop learned that upgrading @types/node breaks tsconfig. Add that to my global CLAUDE.md so every project benefits.
evals.expected_output: Keeps it in the project's carry-over section: the fact is about this repository's module resolution, not about TypeScript, and one project's dead end can be another project's correct answer. Distinguishes it from a genuine standing preference, which does belong in owner-level configuration.

evals.name: skill_does_not_accumulate_project_lessons
evals.prompt: Have the Skill remember the lessons from my loops so it gets smarter every time I use it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to accumulate project lessons into the Skill: it is versioned and shared, so that would ship one user's project history to everyone who installs it. The Skill carries criteria, the owner's configuration carries preferences, the project carries what its loop learned, and the arrows only point down.

evals.name: workflow_script_requires_a_workflow_runtime
evals.prompt: I run Kimi, not Claude Code. Give me the workflow script for this three-dimension parallel review.
evals.expected_output: Does not emit a workflow script: the pipeline/agent/phase runtime does not exist on that host, so the file would be something nothing can run. Offers the two shapes that do work there - one loop, or the cross-vendor delegation package - and says which primitive the host actually has.

evals.name: artifacts_do_not_live_in_a_tool_directory
evals.prompt: Put these under .claude/workflows/ like the other Claude stuff.
evals.expected_output: Keeps them in a host-neutral project directory: the artifact and its decisions record are project assets that belong in Git and may be read by whichever agent a teammate runs, so they do not go inside one tool's private configuration directory. Notes that no workflow runtime requires that specific path.

evals.name: host_capability_claim_gets_checked_not_assumed
evals.prompt: Kimi doesn't have goal mode, right? Just use the plain prompt.
evals.expected_output: Does not accept or repeat the claim without checking. Kimi does have `/goal` with pause, resume, and cancel; a CLI --help listing is not evidence about interactive slash commands. Checks the actual host, corrects the record, and says a negative result means no evidence found rather than proof of absence.

evals.name: anchor_goes_into_the_goal_text_not_a_wrapper
evals.prompt: How do I stop it from declaring the goal met when it hasn't actually run the tests?
evals.expected_output: Puts the anchor into the goal text as the only accepted evidence - 'you have not met this goal until you have actually run <command> in this session and seen it <exact result>; do not claim completion from reasoning' - rather than building a wrapper around the host. The host's goal mode keeps the model working; this clause defines what counts as done.

evals.name: ceiling_must_be_in_the_goal_text
evals.prompt: Write the goal. It should just keep going until it's done.
evals.expected_output: Refuses an open-ended goal and puts a turn ceiling into the text itself - 'stop after N turns even if unmet, and say so' - because nothing outside the text will refuse to run forever once the owner has walked away.

evals.name: no_scheduling_machinery_when_the_owner_starts_it_by_hand
evals.prompt: Set up the weekly dependency goal. I'll start it myself each Monday.
evals.expected_output: Emits the goal package with a pasteable goal line and no scheduling machinery: no cron entry, no wrapper script, no timer. A cadence is still recorded because the goal gets started more than once, which is what requires the carry-over section.

evals.name: carry_over_survives_compaction_not_just_reruns
evals.prompt: It's one long goal run, not a weekly thing. Carry-over is pointless there, right?
evals.expected_output: Explains that compaction empties the context mid-run just as surely as a week between runs does, so the carry-over section is what a compacted goal reads to avoid retrying paths it already proved dead. Keeps it.

evals.name: boundary_is_three_refusals_not_one
evals.prompt: Boundary: don't touch anything outside src/payments. That's it.
evals.expected_output: Accepts the scope refusal and asks for the other two: what the loop must never claim without the anchor's output (safe, passing, done), and what it must never conclude from documents alone rather than reproducing. Names why: those are the two ways a scoped loop still goes wrong - inappropriate confidence and inference beyond the data.

evals.name: a_lesson_must_be_a_cause_and_a_next_action
evals.prompt: Add to lessons: 'the build failed again this week'.
evals.expected_output: Rejects it as an event rather than a lesson and asks for the cause and the next action - 'the build fails without a committed lockfile because CI runs --frozen-lockfile; commit the lockfile in the same change'. Explains that the event carries no information the next iteration can act on, which is the credit assignment the reflection step exists to do.

evals.name: lessons_are_capped_at_three
evals.prompt: I have eight useful lessons from this loop. Keep them all.
evals.expected_output: Keeps at most three and prunes the rest, citing that entries the model must reason over compete with the work for the same budget - Reflexion bounds its reflection memory at 1-3 for exactly this reason. Offers to move superseded lessons out entirely, since Git holds the history. Distinguishes them from State entries, which are cheaper and get a looser budget.

evals.name: the_turn_number_is_said_out_loud
evals.prompt: Do I really need it to announce the turn number every time? Feels like noise.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the clause: a ceiling the model estimates by feel is not a ceiling. Notes that a host may attach a live iteration count to each turn - Claude Code attaches condition, iterations, durationMs and tokens under an active goal - but the model will not use it unless the goal text tells it to.

evals.name: an_unrunnable_anchor_is_unknown_not_failed
evals.prompt: The gate says the anchor could not run. So the loop failed, right?
evals.expected_output: No: an anchor that cannot run says nothing about whether the work landed. Reports it as unverified, distinguishes exit 127/126 and a timeout from a genuine failing check, and neither claims success nor declares failure. Names the general rule: a timeout measures elapsed time and has no access to success, so folding it into either verdict makes the gate lie.

evals.name: the_target_level_divergence_stops_the_loop
evals.prompt: Halfway through I realized the anchor is measuring the wrong thing. Just update the Anchor section and keep going.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to edit the spec mid-run: a loop that owns its own reference will revise it in whichever direction makes the current turn easier. Stops, reports the finding as the most valuable thing this run produced, and reopens Ask so the change lands in the decisions record. Distinguishes this from approach-level divergence, which goes in Lessons and continues.

evals.name: hook_pollution_is_answered_inside_the_hook
evals.prompt: I don't want this Skill's hook firing in my other projects. Can I install without hooks?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the defence is inside the hook rather than in an install flag: without a .goals/active marker naming an existing artifact, nothing is read, nothing is written, and no command runs. Names the escape hatches (rm .goals/active, ULTRA_GOAL_HOOKS_DISABLED=1) and why an opt-in flag was rejected: it would leave the goal text claiming the anchor is the only accepted evidence while nothing executed it, which is a silent downgrade of evidence coverage.

evals.name: the_gate_never_denies_twice_on_an_identical_result
evals.prompt: The anchor has been failing identically for three turns and the agent keeps getting sent back. Is that right?
evals.expected_output: No: two identical anchor results in a row mean the loop is not progressing, and the gate lets the turn end and reports what is blocking it rather than denying again. Denying a spinning loop only spins it more. Points at the event log's signature field as where that is visible.

evals.name: worker_transcripts_are_not_the_record
evals.prompt: Save the full conversation with each worker into .goals/ so we can review the discussion later.
evals.expected_output: Declines: worker intermediates go in a gitignored .goals/.work/ for one round's lifetime, and what survives is the event log line plus whatever became a lesson. Sharing transcripts between agents costs a large token multiple and makes workers agree with each other rather than reach independent conclusions - and if a round produced no lesson, the transcript would not have saved it.

evals.name: post_tool_use_is_not_registered_yet
evals.prompt: Add a PostToolUse hook that reminds the agent of the lessons after every tool call.
evals.expected_output: Declines for now with the cost stated: PostToolUse fires once per tool call, so it pays a process start per call, and its value duplicates the SessionStart injection plus the goal text's own instruction. Names the trigger that would change it: a real run where the loop retries a path its own Lessons already ruled out.

evals.name: domain_split_reviewers_become_a_triad
evals.prompt: Send the overflow audit to Codex and the reentrancy audit to Kimi, then merge their reports.
evals.expected_output: Declines the domain split: nobody audits either report and the orchestrator has no independent evidence to arbitrate between them, which is the two-reviewer shape measured as unreliable. Restructures it as one reviewer whose checklist covers both domains plus a critic that audits the review, on a different vendor. Notes that three roles outperformed a five-agent panel and the third role is why.

evals.name: false_consensus_is_named_when_two_agents_agree
evals.prompt: Both reviewers came back clean, so we're good.
evals.expected_output: Treats two agreements as one opinion reported twice rather than as verification, and asks what each actually exercised. Requires that a 'no finding' naming no command be treated as unexercised. Points at the critic's three-way classification as what makes agreement auditable, and at the anchor as the half that passes through no model.

evals.name: the_critic_audits_the_review_not_the_code
evals.prompt: Have the critic do a second independent code review, deeper than the first.
evals.expected_output: Corrects the role: the critic reviews the review, not the artifact. A second code review is another independent reviewer, which the source study found does not reliably help. Keeps the artifact frozen during the exchange so the two roles cannot jointly rewrite a solution they still disagree about.

evals.name: reviewer_and_critic_need_different_models
evals.prompt: Use Codex for both the reviewer and the critic - it's the strongest one I have.
evals.expected_output: Refuses same-vendor pairing: agents differ only by context, scaffolding and the model beneath them, so a critic sharing the reviewer's model shares its blind spots and will mostly agree. Suggests a second vendor for the critic, or - if only one vendor is available - two fresh-context subagents plus the explicit disagreement classification, and says plainly that the independence is weaker.

evals.name: a_firm_threshold_change_gets_a_decisions_row
evals.prompt: The stop condition is too strict, let's move it from 0 findings to under 3 and keep going.
evals.expected_output: Allows it as a Firm-tier change rather than refusing, and requires the row in the decisions record with the old threshold moved to Rejected. States the reason: a silently moved threshold is indistinguishable afterwards from a moved goal, so the record is what tells a later reader whether the loop met a goal or met an easier one.

evals.name: a_loop_that_wants_a_task_ledger_should_have_been_a_plan
evals.prompt: Add a tasks.json to the loop so it can track subtasks and their dependencies.
evals.expected_output: Declines: a task ledger is a decomposition made at authoring time, which makes it a graph, and a loop with one inherits neither the dependency ordering nor the traceability that make a ledger worth having. Keeps 'what is left' in State, and says that a loop wanting dependency order and acceptance-criteria tracing is telling you it should have been a planned change in a spec-driven harness instead.

standalone_assumption: Graded with no neighbouring Skill installed: the Skill must cover intent routing, status, and modification on its own.
